version: LOCK 42 V1 (9 Nov 2026) - Birana, the wells: the dry well, the long wait, and chapter 2 ends
builds_on: LOCK 34 runner, LOCKs 40-41. Design references (not shown): Quran 2:153, 2:155-157; Abu Dawud 3580 (the briber and the bribe-taker).

birana.name: Birana
birana.text: A green dot on the stony plain: palm trees round a cluster of old wells. This year the water is low and the women queue before dawn.

work.label: Draw water for the queue · 3 coins

birana.title: The well masjid
birana.text: A palm-trunk roof over a floor of packed earth, with the wells just outside the door.
birana.first: An old man fills your cup from the well before you leave. “Pray for rain for us, traveller.”

people.name: Thabit

lines.wary: Thabit doesn't look up from the rope. “Busy.”
lines.friendly: “Water is always there. The question is how deep and how patient you are.”
lines.warm: “You dug with me. That makes you Birana's.”

memory: “Four days in the sand. Most men give up on the second.”

lines.friendly: “I carry forty jars a day. My grandmother carried sixty.”
lines.warm: “The north well is sweet again. The children call it your well. I told them not to.”

people.name: Wahb

lines.wary: Wahb stamps papers without looking up.
lines.friendly: “Permits, permits. Everyone wants to go somewhere.”
lines.warm: Wahb is polite to you now, and careful.

memory: Wahb's hands shake as he stamps. “The qadi has been asking questions. Thanks to you.”
“Ten coins and everything is easy,” Wahb says, and winks.

missions.title: The dry well
missions.button: Thabit is digging the old well deeper

a.text: The north well has gone dry. Thabit thinks there is water further down, but it means days of digging in the heat with no promise. Most men have given up.

choices.label: Pay a labourer to dig · 20 coins

b.text: Three days on there is nothing but damp sand. Thabit sits down, wipes his face and says, “Again tomorrow.”

water.text: Late on the fourth afternoon the sand turns dark and cold, and then the water comes - slowly, then fast. Thabit doesn't cheer. He goes and prays two rak'ahs on the wet sand.

gave.text: You leave Thabit in the hole. A week later you hear he found water on the fifth day.

pay.text: Thabit hires a young man with your coins. They dig together for days.

leave.text: Thabit nods and goes back down the rope.

dug: Dug the north well with Thabit

a.text: To take the north road onward you need a permit stamped by the governor's clerk. Wahb looks at your paper, then at you. “It can take a while. Or - for ten coins - it could be ready today.”

wait.text: “Come back in five days,” Wahb says, and puts your paper at the bottom of the pile.

bribe.text: The paper is stamped before the coins have stopped rolling. A farmer behind you watches every coin.

report.text: The qadi listens, writes something down, and tells you to wait like everyone else.

bribe: Paid Wahb to jump the queue
reported: Reported the clerk who asks for coins

a.text: Five days later Wahb hands you the stamped paper without looking up.

b.text: The north road is open to you.

missions.title: Patience kept
missions.button: Idris wants to hear about the north road

text: Idris listens to all of it: the slow pilgrim, the star, the storm, Khattab, the well and the permit.
“Patience isn't sitting still,” he says. “It's digging one more day.” He nods toward the south gate. “Nahla's beekeepers have a sick child and too few hands. The Gate of Mercy is yours.”

b.text: The next morning the Gate of Mercy is opened for you.
